security.title: Security
security.intro: If you believe you have found a security vulnerability, we want to hear about it. This page explains how to reach us, what is in scope, and what you can expect once you have reported something.
security.canonical: The canonical, always-current version of this policy lives at

noPublicIssue.title: Never report a vulnerability publicly
noPublicIssue.description: A public report tells everyone — including whoever would exploit it — before there is a fix for anyone to upgrade to. Use one of the private channels below.

status.title: Project status
status.description: io2p is at an early stage. APIs and storage formats are still evolving between releases — pin a version and check the release notes before upgrading. An independent security audit has not been carried out yet; until it has, we would rather hear about a problem early than late.

report.title: How to report
report.description: Two private channels, in order of preference.
items: GitHub private vulnerability reporting — open a draft advisory on the affected repository at github.com/maeconomy-org. This is the preferred route: it stays private, gives us somewhere to develop and test the fix, and handles CVE issuance.
Email {email} if you do not have a GitHub account or would rather use email. Please put "security" in the subject line.
Machine-readable contact details are published at io2p.org/.well-known/security.txt, per RFC 9116.

include.title: What to include
include.description: The more of this you can give us, the faster we can confirm and fix it.
items: What the issue is, and what an attacker could achieve with it
Steps to reproduce — ideally a minimal proof of concept
The affected version, commit, or URL
Any relevant configuration, logs, or requests, with secrets redacted

expect.title: What to expect from us
expect.description: We are a small team. If you have not heard back inside the acknowledgement window, please send a follow-up rather than assuming you were ignored.
items: Acknowledgement within 3 business days that your report reached us
An initial assessment — whether we can reproduce it, and our view of the severity — within 10 business days
Progress updates as we work on a fix, and notice before we publish anything
Credit in the advisory, unless you would rather stay anonymous — just tell us which

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: In scope: this application and the io2p services behind it. The following are out of scope.
items: Third-party dependencies — report those upstream. If a dependency issue is reachable through io2p in a way upstream would not consider a vulnerability, that part is in scope.
Any deployed instance we do not operate. io2p is self-hosted software; a particular deployment belongs to whoever runs it.
Findings from automated scanners with no demonstrated impact, missing hardening headers with no exploit path, and reports requiring an already-compromised host or physical access.

harbour.title: Safe harbour
harbour.description: We will not pursue or support legal action against anyone who reports a vulnerability in good faith and follows this policy. If you are unsure whether something you want to test falls inside these lines, ask us first at {email}.
items: Report privately through one of the channels above and give us reasonable time to respond
Act only against your own instance or test data — not other people’s
Do not access, modify, or destroy data that is not yours
Do not degrade the availability of any service
Do not disclose publicly before we have had a chance to release a fix

share.label: What is a share?
share.body: A bundle of objects and processes handed to a group of people at once. It replaced Groups: a group mixed people and resources under one word, a share carries only resources and lists who can see them. Access cascades to children, and you can revoke the whole bundle in one go.

formula.label: What is a formula?
formula.body: A reusable expression bound to a property value, recomputed by the server. Formulas are immutable — to change one you duplicate it and bind the new version, so anything already using the old one keeps its meaning.

constant.label: What is a constant?
constant.body: A shared, versioned number that formulas refer to by name. The version is pinned at the moment you bind it, so publishing a new value never silently changes results that were already computed.

object.label: What is an object?
object.body: Anything you want to track — a machine, a batch, a document. An object carries properties, files, an address and a place in the hierarchy.

process.label: What is a process?
process.body: A step that turns input objects into output objects. Processes are how you record that something was made, moved or transformed, and what it came from.

template.label: What is a template?
template.body: A starting point for new objects: the properties they begin with, including formula recipes and the constants those bind to. Picking one fills the form; you can still change anything.

import.label: How does importing work?
import.body: Bring objects in from a CSV or Excel file in bulk. You map your columns onto object fields once, then the job runs in the background and reports per-row results.

rollupRule.label: What is a rollup rule?
rollupRule.body: A rule that totals one property across everything below an object in the hierarchy. Each distinct descendant counts once, however many paths reach it. Built-in rules apply to everyone; the ones you create apply to your own objects.
